node.name: Power Yoga (11/13)
node.descriptionText:
Join Hayley (GSAS '30) in the Yale Schwarzman Center Dance Studio (located on the lower level of YSC) for an energizing power vinyasa yoga flow.

Yoga mats will be provided but you are more than welcome and encouraged to bring your own. Please bring flexible clothes, a water bottle, and an openness to slowing down for 60 minutes!

If you realize you cannot attend, please cancel your registration so that students from the waitlist may join. 

The Good Life Center is committed to making our events accessible to everyone. At your request, yoga instructors may be able to offer modifications for certain poses during your yoga class. If you require an accommodation or service to fully participate, please contact goodlifecenter@yale.edu.

node.name: Graduate & Professional Student Mixer: Pride & Provisions
node.descriptionText:
Join the Yale LGBTQ Center and Yale Divinity School for Pride & Provisions, a relaxed evening mixer for graduate and professional students from across Yale.

Stop by the Yale LGBTQ Center for wine, beer, cheese, and light provisions while meeting students from across Yale’s graduate and professional schools. Whether you’re looking to make new connections, catch up with friends, or spend some time in community, all Yale G&P students are welcome.

Friday, November 13, 2026 | 5–7 PM
Yale LGBTQ Center | 135 Prospect Street

Presented by the Yale LGBTQ Center in partnership with the Office of Community Engagement and the Office of Student Affairs at Yale Divinity School.

We hope you will stop by to make some new friends and reconnect with old ones as we celebrate our community and welcome in the new school year. We are pleased to provide craft beers as well as non-alcoholic options! (Must be 21+ to drink alcohol: if you would like to, please bring a government ID.) See you there!

This film documents the life of Lina's close friend, acclaimed Syrian novelist Khaled Khalifa, as he navigates his choice of staying in war-torn Damascus. node.name: Treasures from the Yale Film Archive: GUN CRAZY
node.descriptionText:
GUN CRAZY (Joseph H. Lewis, 1950, 35mm, 87 mins)
New print! It’s love at first shot when a gifted marksman meets a carnival sharpshooter whose appetite for excitement proves impossible to resist. Together they race across postwar America chasing the next thrill, the next robbery, the next narrow escape, bound together by desire and self-destruction. An influence on BREATHLESS and BONNIE AND CLYDE, this is “a small but perfectly formed black-and-white masterpiece of flash and trash, unwholesome obsession, and criminal daring” (Peter Bradshaw). 35mm print from the Yale Film Archive, made with thanks to the UCLA Film & Television Archive.

The “Treasures from the Yale Film Archive” series is presented with support from Paul L. Joskow ‘70 M.Phil., ‘72 Ph.D.

node.name: Sealed Off
node.descriptionText:
Join us for an unforgettable evening of theater at the Yale Vermilion Theater FA26 Showcase! 

Set in 1940s Shanghai, Sealed Off begins when a sudden military blockade brings a tram to a halt amid the turmoil of a city at war. Two strangers, Wu Cuiyuan, a university English teaching assistant, and Lü Zongzhen, a bank clerk, find themselves together in the crowded tram. She longs for genuine human contact; he seeks an escape from the monotony of everyday life. As their conversation unfolds, two individuals constrained by family, society, and the roles they are expected to play discover the possibility of connection in this fleeting moment of stillness. But when the blockade is lifted and the tram begins moving again, what will become of them?

Adapted from Eileen Chang's short story of the same name, Sealed Off explores the delicate interplay between truth and illusion in human nature through a chance encounter between two strangers. It also raises questions about the complexities of love: Do we truly fall in love with another person, or do we simply long to be seen through their eyes? Amid the many constraints of reality, can we ever truly reach our authentic selves and one another?

This production is supported by the Grace Hopper College Creative and Performing Arts Award. Production in Chinese (Mandarin) with English subtitles. The event is open to the public, with donations welcome (via Venmo @ChinYuan-Ong). We can’t wait to see you there!

node.name: Sundance Revisited Film Series: BOUND, 30th Anniversary Screening
node.descriptionText:
BOUND (Lana & Lilly Wachowski, 1996, 35mm, 109 mins)
30th anniversary screening! Before reinventing sci-fi, the Wachowskis made their knockout neo-noir debut with a film known for its crackling chemistry, relentless suspense, unabashed eroticism, and style to burn. An ex-con fresh out of prison (Gina Gershon) and her alluring new neighbor (Jennifer Tilly) hatch a plot to steal millions from the mob, but first they’ve got to get around a money-laundering boyfriend (Joe Pantoliano) who fights dirty and suspects everyone. “BOUND is one of those movies that works you up, wrings you out, and leaves you gasping. It's pure cinema, spread over several genres” (Roger Ebert). 35mm print from the Yale Film Archive.

"Sundance Revisited" features a selection of films from our collection that had their American or world premieres at the festival.

node.name: 30 Years of CASA: CASA Board Alumni Careers Panel
node.descriptionText:
The “30 Years of CASA: CASA Alumni & Careers Panel” is an in-person panel discussion and networking session bringing together Yale students, Yale community members, and former board members of the Chinese American Students Association (CASA). Featuring alumni across a range of professions, including medicine, finance, to law, the panel explores post-graduate career opportunities across various professional fields.  

For the first half of the session, panelists will share career advice, discuss strategies for navigating post-graduate life, and reflect on CASA’s historical evolution and growth since its founding in 1995. The structured panel will be followed by an informal Q&A session, fostering direct mentorship and intergenerational connection among Chinese and Asian American students at Yale.
